newsitem.title: USA: Wells Fargo sees Q4 charge of $65 mln.
newsitem.headline: Wells Fargo sees Q4 charge of $65 mln.

text.p: Wells Fargo and Co said it expects to take a fourth quarter charge of $65 million for non-merger related branch closures in 1997.

A spokesman said the charge would be similar to a charge taken in the fourth quarter of 1995 and reflects the bank's policy of expanding its supermarket network and moving customers away from branches.
"Last year in December, we accrued for similar closures in 1996," a spokeswoman said.
Wells Fargo's chief financial officer Rod Jacobs told analysts about the charge on a conference call on Wednesday.
A spokeswoman also confirmed that Jacobs told analysts to expect Wells Fargo to see an increase of $30 million to $40 million to its loan loss provision in the fourth quarter.
The company a reinitiated a loan loss provision during the third quarter for the first time in over a year.

"He told analysts that Wells will see another $30 to $40 million increase in the fourth quarter and gradually build it to a full provision by the fourth quarter of 1997 when it (will sufficiently) cover anticipated losses," the spokeswoman said.
